ticket6_fold.what: Input pack item 5, decided 2026-08-11: ten KPIs each tied to a draft deliverable, and the six expected-impact mappings. The five §2.3 impact claims above are draft lifts and are unchanged.
ticket6_fold.scope_note: The KPI and mapping records are operator decisions, not draft content. Their source_ref cites the input pack, whose in-tier copy ticket 6 placed in source_materials.

impacts.title: Scientific impact
impacts.claim: FIELDWISE provides a framework for agricultural AI evaluated according to temporal + geographic + operational transferability rather than only retrospective accuracy. It additionally establishes a methodological bridge between high-information proximal hyperspectral observations and scalable Sentinel-based prediction.

impacts.title: Environmental impact
impacts.claim: FIELDWISE contributes to the EU-level opportunity for water savings in irrigated agriculture by improving the timing and spatial prioritisation of irrigation decisions. The project does not claim in advance that it will achieve a particular percentage reduction; impact will be quantified from project evidence.

impacts.title: Agricultural and food-production impact
impacts.claim: Water scarcity already produces agricultural yield losses and higher water costs in Europe, while irrigation demand is expected to increase under climate change. Processing tomato provides a high-value horticultural test case in which improved timing can therefore have substantial agronomic and economic relevance.

impacts.title: Technological impact
impacts.claim: FIELDWISE advances the project from a desktop research prototype to a scientifically validated web MVP. External AgroVIR evaluation provides evidence about whether the resulting technology meets actual agricultural software requirements.

impacts.title: European impact
impacts.claim: The MATE-MVCRI architecture directly investigates whether agricultural AI developed in one European environment can be transferred to another. FIELDWISE therefore contributes to a wider European question: how can locally developed agricultural intelligence become reliably transferable rather than remaining confined to the field in which it was trained?

kpis.note: Folded at ticket 6 from operator input pack item 5, accepted 2026-08-11, and completed at ticket 7 with K11, decided 2026-08-12. Eleven KPIs, each measuring something the project controls and delivers, which respects the draft's own refusal (¶243) to set advance numeric targets for water saving. Each names one deliverable that exists in workpackage_seed.json, so phase_05_gate predicate g06_p05 can resolve traceable_to_deliverable from the Phase 5 output. Every accepted deliverable now has a KPI tracing to it. The KPIs are operator decisions, not draft content, and are cited as such.

items.note: Raised in input pack item 5 as a candidate and left undecided there. The operator decided it on 2026-08-12 at the authorisation review, on the ground that D1.3 would otherwise be the one accepted deliverable with no KPI tracing to it. The candidate wording said 'all four steering points' and is amended to five: the second review of the same day added an M27 Career Development Plan review alongside the M27 steering point, because M27 falls inside the placement, which is when non-academic career development is most in play. The five points are M6, M12, M16, M20 and M27, and item 6's review_points carries the same list.

expected_impact_coverage.note: Folded at ticket 6 from operator input pack item 5, decided 2026-08-11. phase_05_gate predicate g06_p04 requires every Tier 2B expected impact to carry at least one mapped project output. All six now map. EI-01, EI-02 and EI-05 map to draft content; EI-03, EI-04 and EI-06 map to measures the operator decided, because the draft addresses none of them. The mapped outputs are deliverables that exist in workpackage_seed.json, except where the measure is an activity rather than a deliverable, which is stated per record.

mappings.expected_impact: Improved employability and career prospects of researchers within academia and beyond.
mappings.mapped_measure: The career progression the draft states in §1.4 and the competences §2.1 lists, made operational by the Career Development Plan (D1.3) and by the non-academic placement at AgroVIR, which adds an inter-sectoral period to the profile.

mappings.expected_impact: Strengthened international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary research collaboration.
mappings.mapped_measure: The Hungary-to-Bulgaria transfer test with MVCRI (international), the AgroVIR evaluation and placement (inter-sectoral), and the two-way transfer between plant physiology and geoinformatics the draft §1.3 describes (interdisciplinary).

mappings.expected_impact: Broadened public engagement with research and innovation.
mappings.mapped_measure: One public field demonstration with AgroVIR farmers, and one public-facing article per year.
mappings.source_ref: Operator input pack item 5, candidate accepted 2026-08-11
mappings.note: Nothing in the draft addresses EI-03. The measure is an operator decision and carries no deliverable id: no deliverable in workpackage_seed.json covers it, and inventing one here would fabricate a project fact. Phase 5 may propose a dissemination deliverable; Phase 3 owns the deliverable list.

mappings.expected_impact: Enhanced convergence of researcher working conditions with the European Charter for Researchers.
mappings.mapped_measure: Charter alignment is evidenced at instrument level by the Career Development Plan (D1.3), by ELTE's open recruitment and researcher-development policies, and by the supervision and training arrangements set out in §1.3.
mappings.source_ref: Operator input pack item 5, accepted 2026-08-11 with the HRS4R claim removed (C8)
mappings.note: The operator confirmed on 2026-08-11 that ELTE does NOT hold the HR Excellence in Research (HRS4R) award, and the claim is removed permanently rather than provisionally. The wording above is final and must not be restored to include HRS4R unless ELTE actually obtains the award. This is the thinnest of the six mappings — it rests on D1.3, institutional policy and §1.3, with no external accreditation — and g06_p04 still passes, because the predicate requires a mapped output and D1.3 is one.

mappings.expected_impact: Increased R&I capacity, output and knowledge transfer among European research organisations.
mappings.mapped_measure: The transfer library, the released predictive engine with its model card, and the adaptation protocol, together with the §1.3 two-way transfer between the fellow and ELTE and the partner contributions of MATE, MVCRI and AgroVIR.

mappings.expected_impact: Enhanced integration of research results into higher education and teaching at host organisations.
mappings.mapped_measure: Co-design and delivery of a full module unit within an ELTE MSc course on Earth observation for agriculture; primary supervision of one ELTE MSc thesis to completion; co-supervision of the field-experiment component of one PhD student's work.
mappings.source_ref: Operator input pack item 5, raised measure adopted 2026-08-11 (C7)
mappings.note: This replaces the original candidate of one guest module and one co-supervised thesis. The operator raised it once the CV showed five years of university teaching, so the measure is a transfer of an existing strength into a new discipline, institution and language of instruction rather than a competence to acquire. Two consequences carried from item 5, neither of which blocks a gate: the workload lands in a 3.0 person-month cross-cutting allocation and may need to be stated as sitting inside the training allocation, and primary supervision of an ELTE MSc thesis may require a formal ELTE status the fellow will not automatically hold. If it does, the measure drops to co-supervision and the module unit carries the ambition. Like EI-03, the measure carries no deliverable id.
